CITY OF INGLEWOOD

City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor (Planning Commission & Staff)
1 West Manchester Boulevard

  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Until further notice, meetings of the Inglewood Planning Commission will be
conducted pursuant to California Government Code section 54953(e), which
allows the City to use teleconferencing for members of the public to access
a meeting and to address the legislative body via a call-in option.

CALL-IN OPTION
1. Members of the public who wish to attend the Planning Commission Meeting
of July 6, 2022 and address the Planning Commission must use the call-in
option noted below:
Instructions: Dial one of the Phone Numbers below and when prompted,
enter the Access Code:
  Phone Number: 888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 6568755#
In the event of a disruption which prevents the City from broadcasting the
meeting to the public using the call-in option, or in the event of a
disruption within the City’s control which prevents the public from offering
public comments using the call-in option, the Planning Commission shall take
no further action on items appearing on the meeting agenda until public
access to the meeting via the call-in option is restored.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City also provides alternative methods for members of the public to
submit comments and/or to observe a public meeting. The following
alternative methods are provided to the public as a matter of convenience
only and the disruption in service to any alternative method does not
preclude the Planning Commission from taking further action on an agenda
item. In the event of a disruption to any alternative method below members
of the public should use the call-in option above.
2. Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may
choose to submit comments for consideration by the Planning Commission by
sending  them  to  Mindy  Wilcox,  AICP,  Planning  Manager  at
mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the
Planning Commission prior to consideration of the agenda, comments must be
received prior to 12:00 P.M. on the day of the meeting. Correspondence
should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after
12:00 P.M. and prior to the close of the public hearing will be made part
of the official public record of the meeting.
3. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video.  Please
check with your cable provider for details
  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video at
https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

Accessibility: If you will require special accommodations due to a
disability, please contact the Planning Division Office at (310) 412-5230,
One Manchester Boulevard, 4th Floor, Inglewood, California 90301.  All
requests for accommodations must be received 48 hours prior to the day of
the hearing.
Español: "Si no entiende esta noticia o si necesita más información, favor
de llamar a este número (310) 412-5230."

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, JULY 6, 2022

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, July 6, 2022, in the Council
Chambers on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Commissioner Shaw-Williams, the meeting was called
to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams
  Chairman Larry Springs

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Michael Pan, Assistant City Attorney
  Arturo Salazar, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Planner
  Angel Leon-Martell, Assistant Planner
  Christine Rivera, Assistant Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner
  Reyes Gonzales, Intern Planning Technician
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox stated:
 Item 6a had a revision and the revised item 6a was placed on
  the City’s website prior to tonight’s meeting along with being
  given to the planning commissioners.
 Staff has received no communications from the public on any
  items before the Planning Commission this evening.
 Introduction of newest Planning Division Intern, Reyes Gonzales.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None (Confirmed by AT&T Operator)

(5) MINUTES APPROVAL:

Chairman Springs called for a vote to approve June 1, 2022 minutes.

Motion to Approve June 1, 2022 Minutes by Commissioner Shaw-
Williams and second by Commissioner Trejo.

The motion passed with the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams, and
  Chairman Springs.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 6, 2022

(6) PUBLIC HEARINGS:

6A. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2022-004 (SP-2022-004), 614 EAST HYDE
PARK BOULEVARD.

A public hearing to consider an application by Nuritsa Poghosian
for Special Use Permit No. 2022-004 (SP-2022-004) to amend
Conditions of Approval for SP-2017-006, for a proposed 18-bed
community care residential health facility on an 11,425 square-
foot, R-3 (Multiple-family Residential) zoned property at 614 East
Hyde Park Boulevard.

Mr. Angel Leon-Martell,  Assistant  Planner  made  the  staff
presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff several questions –
 Hasn’t this item come before the Planning Commission once
  before?
 He also asked why these new changes to the project’s setup?
 Why has no business license been applied for, as of yet?
  - Mr. Leon-Martell responded to Commissioner Rice.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 Will there be any drug and mental health counseling held at the
  site?
 When did the applicant determine that there needed to be this
  change in their request to apply for their business license?
  - Mr. Leon-Martell responded to Commissioner Trejo.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to give their name and talk
about their project.

Mr. Robert Cole spoke to the Planning Commission via telephone
regarding the project and answered questions from the Planning
Commission.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the Planning Commission to
address the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant –
 When does the applicant expect to start construction on their
  facility?
  - Mr. Cole responded to Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant –
 Clarification regarding condition no. 5, does this include staff
  members assisting the patients with regards to personal lavatory
  issues?
  - Mr. Cole responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant –
 Based on the statement given earlier about no mental health or
  psychiatric services would be administered at the facility, what
  measures will be taken for staff to be trained to be able to
  recognize if there is the need for any of the residents to have
  psychiatric or mental health therapeutic services?
   Mr. Cole responded to Commissioner Shaw-Williams’ question.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 6, 2022
Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to
speak either for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:

None (Confirmed by the AT&T Operator).

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and called for a
motion.

MOTION:

Commissioner Rice made the motion to affirm categorical exemption
EA-CE-2022-060 and adopt the attached resolution approving SP-
2022-004 subject to 13 conditions, and/or add conditions as deemed
appropriate and it was second by Commissioner Shaw-Williams,
Resolution No. 1933

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A
  CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT TO AMEND CONDITIONS
  OF APPROVAL FOR SP-2017-006, FOR A PROPOSED
  18-BED COMMUNITY CARE RESIDENTIAL HEALTH
  FACILITY ON AN 11,425 SQUARE-FOOT, R-3
  (MULTIPLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL) ZONED PROPERTY
  AT 614 EAST HYDE PARK BOULEVARD.

Be Approved.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

6B. ZONING CODE AMENDMENT 2022-002 (ZCA-2022-002), CITYWIDE.

A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment 2022-002 (ZCA-
2022-002) to modify miscellaneous regulations in Chapter 12 of the
Inglewood Municipal Code related to Environmental Review, Parking
Alternatives, and Cosmetology Use Separation Citywide.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner David Rice asked staff –
 How will private businesses which now have “suites” available
  for leasing, be able to operate when this update to the ZCA
  takes effect?
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 Based upon what is being proposed by the Hollywood Park project
  how will this new ZCA effect their decisions and/or will it
  affect their upcoming projects at all?
 Feels that any ZCA’s for the City must be reflected also at
  Hollywood Park and is concerned that it might not be so.
 Will any requests for Beauty Salons or Cosmetology issues be
  brought before the Planning Commission prior to approval for
  use, regardless of who the applicant will be?
  - Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.
  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 6, 2022

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to
speak either for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
None (Confirmed by the AT&T Operator).

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and ask for final
comments and/or questions to staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
 With the City’s present Zoning Code, one applicant lost over
  $40,000.00 on a project, due to antiquated Zoning Code for the
  City and that is a great concern.
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Commissioner Trejo made a statement to staff –
 Thank you to staff for taking the time now to deal with the
  Zoning Code as it effects the City overall and these changes
  need to be made in order to bring our Codes up to date.

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and called for a
motion.

MOTION:

Commissioner Shaw-Williams made the motion to affirm Environmental
Impact Report Addendum EA-CE-2022-072, and adopt a resolution
recommending City Council’s adoption of ZCA-2022-002 and was
seconded by Commissioner Trejo that Resolution No. 1934

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AND
  RECOMMENDING TO THE CITY COUNCIL FOR APPROVAL
  ZONING CODE AMENDMENT ZCA 2022-002 TO MODIFY
  MISCELLANEOUS REGULATIONS IN CHAPTER 12 OF THE
  INGLEWOOD  MUNICIPAL  CODE  RELATED  TO
  ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW, PARKING ALTERNATIVES,
  AND COSMETOLOGY USE SEPARATION CITYWIDE.

Be approved.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Yeas:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams, and
  Chairman Springs.

Ms. Wilcox explained there is no appeal process.

(7) NON-PUBLIC HEARING

7A. DESIGN REVIEW NO. 2022-007 (DR-2022-007), 3200-3216 WEST
MANCHESTER BOULEVARD.

A Design Review to approve a 1,007 square-foot addition, exterior
alterations, and signs affixed to the tower element of an existing
one-story commercial building located within the Art Deco Overlay
for 3200-3216 West Manchester Boulevard.

Mr. Arturo Salazar, Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 6, 2022

Commissioner Trejo asked Staff –
  Will the details for the sign be given to the Planning
  Commission later or how will the sign be designed, will it be
  lit, will there be an actual crown on the top, maybe be in
  neon?
  Possible to pass along to the applicant to do a neon styled
  sign with back-light illuminations, as that will be a nice
  touch for the design of the sign.
  - Mr. Salazar responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Chairman Springs asked Staff –
  About the history of the building and when was it built?
  Is this a purchase of the building by the applicant or lease
  Does the parking lot to the south of the building belong to
  the City or property owner?
  - Mr. Salazar responded to Chairman Springs’ questions.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to give their name and talk
about their project.

Ms. Margaret Taylor, Planning Consultant, introduced Mr. Teo
Hunter, Co-Founder, Mr. Smith, Architect and Ms. Benyvette
Robinson, Applicant/Co-Founder, and then spoke to the Planning
Commission via telephone regarding the project and answered
questions from the Planning Commission.

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and ask for final
comments and/or questions to staff.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant –
 Having seen this particular building over the years, from the
  Bowling Alley to its previous status of the Adult Daycare
  facility, what kind of restaurant will this be and is this a
  chain of restaurants? Not familiar with the name Crown and Hops.
  - Mr. Hunter responded to Commissioner Patrick’s question.
 Parking has always been an issue at that site, now that area is
  by permitted parking only, how will this establishment guarantee
  parking for 14 cars?
   Ms. Taylor responded to Commissioner Patrick’s question.
 Will there be the sale of spirits at this restaurant, as they
  have applied to sell Beer and Wine?
   Ms. Taylor responded to Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant –
 Glazing on the windows on the north side of the building on
  Manchester side, will they be transparent or obscured?
   Ms. Taylor responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.
   Mr. Smith, Architect also responded to Commissioner Rice’s
  question.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant –
 Will this be a white “Table-Cloth” restaurant or a casual styled
  typed restaurant?
   Mr. Hunter responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
   Ms. Taylor responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant –
 What is the proposed time-frame for the completion of this
  restaurant project?
   Ms. Taylor responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

  5
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
July 6, 2022

Chairman Springs asked the applicant –
  With the serving of Beer and Wine, will this be imported beer,
  or a variety of different beers?
  With the Parking lot to the south-side of the building
  belonging to the property, now being utilized by the
  neighboring residents, how will the applicant insure that their
  customers will have ample parking spaces?
  Hours of operation for this establishment?
  - Mr. Hunter responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
  - Ms. Taylor responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
  - Ms. Robinson responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant –
 Is this the first Crown and Hops restaurant or are there others?
   Ms. Robinson responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Chairman Springs closed the hearing and called for a motion.

MOTION:

Commissioner Trejo made the motion to affirm Categorical Exemption
EA-CE-2022-068; and adopt the attached resolution approving DR-
2022-007 subject to 13 conditions, and/or add conditions as deemed
appropriate and was seconded by Commissioner Shaw-Williams that
Resolution No. 1935

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AN
  APPLICATION  BY  BENYVETTE  ROBINSON,
  REPRESENTING CROWNS & HOPS, FOR DESIGN REVIEW
  NO. 2022-007 TO APPROVE A 1,007 SQUARE-FOOT
  ADDITION, EXTERIOR ALTERATIONS AND SIGNS
  AFFIXED TO A TOWER ELEMENT OF AN EXISTING ONE-
  STORY COMMERCIAL BUILDING IN THE ART DECO
  OVERLAY ZONE ON AN APPROXIMATELY 21,900
  SQUARE-FOOT, C-2 (GENERAL COMMERCIAL) ZONED
  SITE LOCATED AT 3200-3216 WEST MANCHESTER
  BOULEVARD.

Be approved.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

(8) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None, (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

Chairman Springs closed the meeting to the public and asked for
the Planning Commission Initiatives.

(9) COMMISSION INITIATIVES:

Commissioner Patrick –
 Wishing everyone a very Happy and Safe Summer.
